questions.question: Which of the following is one of the three conditions a noun must meet to take Category 1 i'rāb (ḍamma in raf', fatḥa in naṣb, kasra in jarr)?
options: The noun must be muḍāf to a definite noun
The noun must be a proper noun (ism 'alam)
The noun must be mufrad (singular)
The noun must be masculine (mudhakkar)
questions.explanation: The three conditions are: (1) mufrad (singular), (2) munsarif (accepts tanwīn and kasra), and (3) ṣaḥīḥ in the naḥw sense — its final letter is not a ḥarf 'illah (ا، و، ي).

questions.question: In naḥw, a noun ending in wāw or yā' with sukūn on the preceding letter is given which classification?
options: اسْمٌ مَنْقُوص
جَارٍ مَجْرَى الصَّحِيحِ
غَيْرُ مُنْصَرِف
اسْمٌ مَقْصُور
questions.explanation: A noun ending in wāw or yā' with sukūn on the preceding letter — such as دَلْوٌ or ظَبْيٌ — is called جَارٍ مَجْرَى الصَّحِيحِ ('acting like a ṣaḥīḥ noun') and follows Category 1 i'rāb.

questions.question: Which of the following is one of the four conditions required for أَسْمَاءُ السِّتَّةِ to be declined with wāw, alif, and yā'?
options: The noun must be in the dual (tasniyah) form
The noun must be muḍāf to yā' al-mutakallim
The noun must be singular (muwāḥada), not dual or plural
The noun must be used as the subject (mubtadaʾ) of the sentence
questions.explanation: One of the four conditions is muwāḥada — the noun must be singular. If it is dual or plural, the special wāw/alif/yā' i'rāb does not apply.

questions.question: What single feature distinguishes the dual رَأَيْتُ مُسْلِمَيْن from the plural رَأَيْتُ مُسْلِمِين?
options: Whether the noon is sākin or mutaḥarrik
The presence or absence of the noon at the end
The length of the alif in the root
The harakah before the yā' — fatḥa for dual, kasra for plural
questions.explanation: رَأَيْتُ مُسْلِمَيْن has fatḥa before yā' (tasniyah — 'I saw two Muslims'), while رَأَيْتُ مُسْلِمِين has kasra before yā' (jam' muzakkar sālim — 'I saw many Muslims'). Confusing the two entirely changes the meaning.

questions.question: When a غَيْرُ مُنْصَرِفٌ noun is majrūr, what marker does it carry instead of kasra?
options: fatḥa
ḍamma
tanwīn
sukūn
questions.explanation: A ghayr munsarif noun rejects both tanwīn and kasra; when majrūr, fatḥa substitutes for the kasra it cannot take.

questions.question: Which of the following is one of the أَسْمَاءُ السِّتَّةِ?
options: رَجُلٌ (man)
بَيْتٌ (house)
فَمٌ (mouth)
يَدٌ (hand)
questions.explanation: The six nouns are أَبٌ (father), أَخٌ (brother), حَمٌ (father-in-law), فَمٌ (mouth), هَنٌ, and ذُو (possessor of).

questions.question: نُونُ التَّثْنِيَةِ always carries _____, while the noon of jam' muzakkar sālim always carries _____.
options: ḍamma; kasra
kasra; fatḥa
fatḥa; kasra
sukūn; fatḥa
questions.explanation: نُونُ التَّثْنِيَةِ is always maksūr (kasra), while noon al-jam' is always maftūḥ (fatḥa) — this distinction allows you to tell dual from plural in the naṣb/jarr forms.

questions.question: According to Al-Baqarah 2:7, which of the following is one of the three faculties described as sealed?
options: الْعَقْل (the intellect)
اللِّسَان (the tongue)
الأَيْدِي (the hands)
الأَبْصَار (the eyesight)
questions.explanation: The three sealed faculties are the hearts (الْقُلُوب), the hearing (السَّمْع), and the eyesight (الأَبْصَار). The sealing is a spiritual metaphor (majāz), not a physical condition.

questions.question: Why did Allah devote 13 full verses to the Munafiqeen in Surah Al-Baqarah — more than to the Mu'minoon or the Kafireen?
options: Because of the great danger (خَطَر عَظِيم) they posed from within and the great harm (ضَرَر كَبِير) they could inflict
Because the Munafiqeen were more numerous than the Mu'minoon in Madinah
Because the Munafiqeen asked the Prophet ﷺ many questions requiring detailed answers
Because Allah wished to teach the Mu'minoon how to refute Munafiq arguments
questions.explanation: Allah devoted 13 verses to the Munafiqeen because of the great danger and great harm they pose to the Muslim community from within. After these verses, two parables (مَثَلَان) further expose the inner darkness of their souls.

questions.question: In what sense do the Munafiqeen deceive only themselves (وَمَا يَخْدَعُونَ إِلَّا أَنفُسَهُمْ)?
options: The evil consequence (وَبَال) of their deception returns to them alone
They cannot truly deceive Allah, so technically they deceive no one at all
Their deception is never effective against the believers
They are so foolish they eventually contradict themselves in public
questions.explanation: The evil consequence (وَبَال) of their deception returns to them alone — they are the ones harmed most by their own nifaq. They cannot perceive this due to their excessive heedlessness (تَمَادِي غَفْلَتِهِمْ) and the completeness of their foolishness.

questions.question: In أَلَا إِنَّهُمْ هُمُ الْمُفْسِدُونَ, what grammatical role does the pronoun هُمْ play?
options: It is ضَمِيرُ الْفَصْل, restricting the predicate exclusively to this subject
It functions as the subject (mubtadaʾ) of an embedded nominal sentence
It emphasizes plurality, indicating there are many Munafiqeen
It is a pronoun substituting for أَنَّهُمْ mentioned earlier in the verse
questions.explanation: هُمْ here is ضَمِيرُ الْفَصْل placed between the mubtadaʾ and khabar — it restricts the predicate exclusively to this subject, meaning 'it is they and none other' who are the corrupters.

questions.question: What does نُورُ الْبَصِيرَة refer to, according to the mufassirūn?
options: The light of inner insight and imān in the heart
The light of knowledge acquired through formal Islamic study
The physical light perceived by the eyes in darkness
The light of Quranic recitation that illuminates the believer's path
questions.explanation: نُورُ الْبَصِيرَة is the light of inner insight and imān. Accumulated sins gradually obscure it; once lost, there is no pathway (مَسْلَك) for imān to enter or for kufr to exit the heart.

questions.question: What does the word وَبَال mean in the context of the Munafiqeen deceiving only themselves?
options: The evil or bad consequence of one's own action returning upon oneself
The outward sin visible to other believers
The divine punishment specifically reserved for the Day of Judgment
Spiritual blindness that prevents self-awareness
questions.explanation: وَبَال means the evil/bad consequence or result — the harmful outcome of one's own action returning upon oneself. The Munafiqeen's deception harms themselves most.

questions.question: What is the grammatical function of the particle أَلَا called in Arabic?
options: حَرْفُ النَّفْيِ (particle of negation)
الْمُنَبِّه (alerting/warning particle that draws the listener's attention)
حَرْفُ الشَّرْطِ (conditional particle)
حَرْفُ الِاسْتِفْهَامِ (interrogative particle)
questions.explanation: أَلَا is called الْمُنَبِّه — the alerting/warning particle that draws the listener's full attention before an emphatic statement, as in Allah's refutation of the Munafiqeen in Ayah 12.

questions.question: How many of water's three qualities (color, taste, smell) must be altered by a foreign substance before the water becomes impermissible for ṭahāra?
options: Only taste and smell matter — color alone does not affect the ruling
Even one change makes it impermissible
All three must be changed
Two or more must be changed
questions.explanation: If two or more of the three qualities are altered by a foreign substance, the water is no longer permissible for ṭahāra. If only one quality is changed by a permissible additive such as soap or saffron, ṭahāra remains valid.

questions.question: Which of the following requires ghusl?
options: مَذْي (pre-seminal fluid released during foreplay)
مَنِي (seminal fluid discharged with desire/shahwa)
وَادِي (fluid sometimes seen after urination)
Any discharge that becomes visible after urination
questions.explanation: مَنِي discharged with desire (shahwa) necessitates ghusl. مَذْي and وَادِي only break wuḍū — wash the affected area and make wuḍū; no ghusl is required for either.

questions.question: At what exact moment does water become مَاءٌ مُسْتَعْمَل?
options: When it first comes into contact with a limb being washed
When it is poured from the container into the hand
The moment it drips off/leaves the body after use
After the full wuḍū or ghusl is completed
questions.explanation: Water acquires the status of musta'mal the moment it drips off/leaves the body — while still on the skin it remains ṭahūr. This precise point is the operative Ḥanafī ruling.

questions.question: What is the Ḥanafī response to Imam Malik's use of the Bi'r Budha'a hadith for small stagnant bodies of water?
options: The Ḥanafīs accept the hadith but limit it to wells located in Madinah
Bi'r Budha'a had an underground stream continuously replenishing it — it was effectively flowing water, not stagnant
The hadith applies only to wells, not to ponds or rivers
The Bi'r Budha'a hadith is considered weak (ḍa'īf) and inadmissible
questions.explanation: Bi'r Budha'a had an underground stream continuously replenishing it — it was effectively flowing water (mā' jārī). The hadith therefore cannot override the rule for genuinely still, stagnant small bodies of water.

questions.question: Which of the following correctly describes مَاءٌ طَهُور?
options: It is pure only when combined with a cleansing agent such as soap
It is impure but can be purified through boiling or filtering
It is pure in itself and capable of purifying others
It is pure in itself but cannot purify others
questions.explanation: طَهُور has two properties: (1) pure in itself and (2) capable of purifying others. Examples include rainwater, river water, well water, seawater, and spring water.

questions.question: Under the Ḥanafī ruling, مَاءٌ مُسْتَعْمَل may be used for which of the following?
options: Performing ghusl after janābah
Performing wuḍū before ṣalāh
Renewing an existing wuḍū
Irrigation, cooking, and general household use
questions.explanation: Mā' musta'mal is ṭāhir but not muṭahhar — it may not be used for wuḍū or ghusl, but it may be used for istiñjā', irrigation, cooking, and general purposes.

questions.question: Which scholar appears in BOTH الشَّيْخَانِ and الصَّاحِبَانِ?
options: Imam Abu Yusuf
Imam Abu Hanifa
Imam Zufar
Imam Muhammad
questions.explanation: الشَّيْخَانِ = Imam Abu Hanifa + Imam Abu Yusuf; الصَّاحِبَانِ = Imam Abu Yusuf + Imam Muhammad. Imam Abu Yusuf is the shared scholar between both terms.
